title: Dimmer
description: Send a number from your computer to set an LED's brightness.

steps.clip: You need: an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 1 × 220 Ω resistor, 1 × LED, and some jumper wires.
Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard. Put its two legs in two different columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED — without it the LED can burn out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: Run a wire from one leg of the 220 Ω resistor to pin 9 on the Arduino.
hints: Put the wire in any hole in the same column as the leg.
Pin 9 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.

steps.clip: Put the LED in: the long leg in the same column as the 220 Ω resistor's other leg, the short leg in the next column.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode). Backwards, the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are connected — no wire needed.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip:
Two wires:
1. The Arduino's GND pin → the blue − row at the bottom of the breadboard.
2. The LED's short leg → that same row.
hints: GND is the minus side of the circuit.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. Each character you send in the Serial Monitor sets the brightness by its code: 'A' (65) is dim, 'z' (122) is brighter.
